claims.text: Neither combination met the historical-control futility criterion; this is not proof of benefit versus placebo.
The mortality comparison among all 86 randomized participants was uncertain and did not reach statistical significance.
Stopping study treatment did not mean loss of clinical follow-up.
Rash was reported more often in the celecoxib-creatine arm in the exploratory analysis of all 86 participants.

Depression was reported more often in the minocycline-creatine arm in the exploratory analysis of all 86 participants.
Clinical creatinine elevations occurred in both arms; the trial does not establish safety relative to no treatment.

reviewInputs.answer: Select between minocycline-creatine and celecoxib-creatine for further ALS research using a prespecified six-month ALSFRS-R selection rule. Secondary futility analyses used historical controls. This is phase II screening, not a placebo-controlled efficacy trial.

reviewInputs.answer: Adults at 17 US centers, aged 21-85 years, with possible, laboratory-supported probable, probable or definite ALS; FVC at least 60% predicted and weakness onset within five years. Riluzole had to be stable for at least 30 days if used. Figure 1 shows 108 assessed, 18 excluded, four withdrawals before randomization and 86 randomized: 47 celecoxib-creatine and 39 minocycline-creatine. The primary pool was the first 60, with 30 in each arm. Eligibility exclusions are applicability restrictions, not automatically contraindications.

sourceLocators.section: Patients and methods: Patients; Study design

reviewInputs.answer: Both arms received 10 g creatine powder twice daily. One added 100 mg minocycline twice daily; the other added 400 mg celecoxib twice daily. These were the tested six-month regimens, not clinical recommendations. Identical capsules supported blinding; adverse events could prompt dose reduction, a temporary holiday or permanent discontinuation.

Two concurrent active combinations, each containing creatine; no concurrent placebo or untreated group. Historical combined-arm data from a separate gabapentin trial provided the secondary futility benchmark only.

sourceLocators.section: Patients and methods: Patients; Study design

reviewInputs.answer: The primary outcome was six-month ALSFRS-R decline used for selection. FVC, Timed Up and Go, quality of life, death/tracheostomy/chronic ventilation, adverse events, laboratory studies and ECGs were assessed as secondary safety measures. Function matters to patients, but this design does not provide definitive efficacy estimation.

Eight located candidates capture primary decline and selection, futility, mortality, treatment discontinuation/adherence and four specific safety events among all 86. Primary mean decline was 6.47 with minocycline-creatine versus 5.27 with celecoxib-creatine; the reported absolute difference of 1.200 exceeded the selection threshold of 1.035. This is not a conventional superiority test, pooled benefit estimate or clinical grade.

reviewInputs.answer: Of the primary 60, 58 had measured six-month scores and two minocycline-creatine deaths received score zero. Patients stopping treatment continued follow-up; authors report no follow-up dropouts beyond endpoint death. Figure 1 separately reports four withdrawals before randomization. Table II states 14 missing TUG observations, but placement of n=72 beside quality of life needs adjudication before extracting those secondary denominators. Table V follow-up n=85 and mixed percentage denominators also remain unresolved.

reviewInputs.answer: Scheduled clinical, laboratory and ECG monitoring and independent safety monitoring were used. Selected Table IV event counts are located. Table III reported no significant differences in totals, and Table V laboratory abnormalities are distinct from clinically significant creatinine events. Continued table headers and some laboratory denominators require independent audit; absence of rare events cannot establish safety.

reviewInputs.answer: Randomization was stratified by center and progression rate; capsules were blinded and no code breaks were reported. Limits include the small selection design, active comparators and historical benchmark, overenrollment beyond the first 60, death scores imputed as zero, selected secondary missing-data imputation and multiple exploratory safety comparisons. The study did not compare doses or formally sample blood/CSF drug exposure.

reviewInputs.answer: These findings concern the tested ALS combinations, eligibility, six-month screening purpose and separate first-60/all-86 analyses. They do not establish minocycline-alone efficacy, long-term survival, optimal dose or benefit versus standard care or placebo.
